subject: history_social
passage: Along the streets of Pompeii, the Roman town buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE, archaeologists have found well over a thousand painted notices urging residents to vote for particular candidates in local elections. Many of the notices were painted by professional sign writers, whom candidates or their supporters paid for the work. The notices appear not only near the grand houses of wealthy families but also along ordinary commercial streets, on the walls of bakeries, workshops, and taverns frequented by laborers and shopkeepers. Taken together, these findings suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: candidates probably expected many ordinary passersby to be able to read the notices.
choices.B: only wealthy citizens were allowed to vote in Pompeii's local elections.
choices.C: most residents of Pompeii could write as well as read.
choices.D: the sign writers chose where to paint the notices without consulting the candidates.

explanation.why: Candidates paid professionals to paint these notices, so they presumably wanted them read. Placing them on streets and shops used by laborers and shopkeepers would make sense only if candidates believed many ordinary people could read them.
explanation.A: Correct. Paying to place written appeals where laborers and shopkeepers passed suggests candidates expected many of those people to read them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Painting appeals on walls frequented by laborers and shopkeepers suggests candidates sought ordinary residents' votes, not only the wealthy's.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Painted notices say something about reading, not writing, and professionals did much of the painting.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says candidates or supporters paid for the notices but says nothing about who chose their locations.
